entries.proposition: No child was measured: the DM-1 patients were 13.8 to 34.9 years (mean 20.9), 16 in total; the healthy volunteers were aged 60 to 74.
entries.snippet: The age of patients included in the analysis ranged from 13.8 to 34.9 years [mean: 20.9, s.d. = 5.9 years]

entries.proposition: Tideglusib was given as 400 or 1000 mg once daily in the DM-1 phase II study for 12 weeks (two dose points, 8 patients each).
entries.snippet: Subjects were assigned to either 400 mg or 1000 mg q.d. doses of tideglusib according to a 1:1 ratio.

entries.proposition: PK evidence: the model says bioavailability is dose-dependent but with a two-level step (400 mg versus higher), not a continuous curve.
entries.snippet: Instead, bioavailability and absorption rate constant were dichotomized into two levels, with exposure data following a 400 mg dose as reference.

entries.proposition: Abstract and Conclusions call the dependence "dose-dependent bioavailability" and a less-than-proportional rise in exposure; the model parameterises that with two levels fitted to 6 healthy-adult dose groups and 2 patient dose levels, so no threshold or gradation is located.
entries.snippet: Our parameterisation suggests that oral bioavailability decreases with increasing doses, even though we have not been able to quantify these changes in a continuous manner.

entries.proposition: Body weight as a covariate: the text claims higher exposure at lower weight in both populations.
entries.snippet: Despite the relatively large interindividual variability, it seems that higher exposure is expected to occur in subjects with lower body weight (Figure 5).

entries.proposition: Pharmacokinetic extrapolation to children assumes the adult 1000 mg exposure is the efficacy target and that PK-PD is the same in children.
entries.snippet: assuming that the exposures observed in adults and adolescents following 1000 mg q.d. dose are clinically relevant and can be considered as a target for efficacy

entries.proposition: Paediatric clearance maturation is not modelled: the authors state no maturation function and no age-dependent exponent were included, and the primary metabolic route in vivo is incompletely known.
entries.snippet: neither a maturation function nor an age-dependent allometric exponent were included in the simulated scenarios

entries.proposition: The model scales on weight only (5 to 75 kg uniform virtual population of 71 per band), so an infant of 5 kg is predicted on allometry alone.
entries.snippet: Scenarios consisted of a virtual population of 71 patients per weight band, and dose level, considering a uniform distribution of weight ranging from 5 to 75 kg.

entries.proposition: No safety or tolerability result of tideglusib in any child is reported; the tolerability reference for the lower-dose scenario is an adult 400 mg value, said to address tolerability concerns in the youngest.
entries.snippet: For completeness, to address potential tolerability concerns in the youngest subjects, a weight-banded regimen has been explored considering the 400 mg as the reference dose in adults (Table S4).

entries.proposition: Liver signals: transaminase elevations were seen with earlier formulations given with food, twice daily and at highest doses; the authors reason this may reflect GSK3 inhibition and liver repair, which is interpretation.
entries.snippet: Abnormalities in serum transaminases have been observed, particularly in a twice-daily dosing regimens, when the drug was administered with food and at the highest doses.

entries.proposition: Food: the text finds no effect of food or meal type with 30 records spread over meal categories of 1 to 3 patients each.
entries.snippet: There was no evidence of an effect of food or meal type on the predicted exposure to tideglusib.
entries.anchor: Results / Influence of Type and Time of Food Intake

entries.proposition: Sponsor interest: three authors are employees of the sponsor and the sponsor funded two authors.
entries.snippet: Joseph Horrigan, Alison McMorn, and Stuart Evans are all employees for AMO Pharma, who were the Sponsors of this clinical trial.

entries.proposition: Supplement Table S4 proposes a lower weight-banded titration (100 mg below 20 kg, 200 mg to 45 kg, 400 mg above); simulation outputs list the share above the adult 95th percentile (0.00 to 2.04 percent). A recorded observation of a simulation, not a dose.
entries.snippet: Proposed lower weight-banded dosing regimen for tideglusib in paediatric and adult patients with DM-1

entries.proposition: Fig 5 (360 ppi raster): at 400 mg (left) AUC and Cmax are flat against body weight with a near-zero slope (DM-1 n = 8, healthy n = 9), while at 1000 mg (right) the dashed trend slopes down (AUC about 3600 at 45 kg to about 1100 at 120 kg) resting on eight DM-1 points whose spread (1600 to 5700 at 45-75 kg) exceeds the trend; the two highest points (about 6100 healthy, 5700 patient) are at 60 and 75 kg. So the weight relation is visible at the higher dose only.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] 400 mg trend ~flat; 1000 mg trend slopes from ~3600 to ~1100; 8 blue points

entries.proposition: Fig 6 (160 dpi page 14): simulated AUC and Cmax for weight bands 5 to 70 kg; the 5th-95th whiskers of the 100 mg band at 5-10 kg and the 200 mg band reach about 2000 ng/mL for Cmax; medians fall inside the adult reference band in most bands and below it for the smallest 100 mg weights; plotted points are simulation, not observation.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Cmax medians ~600 to 1100; whiskers to ~2300 at 20 kg
entries.qualifies_needle: assuming that the exposures observed in adult

entries.proposition: Fig 4 (160 dpi page 12): predicted AUC and Cmax by time of first meal, 400 and 1000 mg, below and above 60 kg; three meal types with 1-3 subjects per cell; the 1000 mg <60 kg cell sits at about 3400-4500 AUC and the >=60 kg cell near 1700 except one at about 5700, so weight and dose differences are larger than any meal-type difference visible.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] AUC 1000 mg <60 kg ~3400-4500; >=60 kg ~1700 with one ~5700
